question:
AB is a common tangent to both the circles in the given figure. Find the distance (correct to two decimal places) between the centres of the two circles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/337cb28fb01d27293af53cb76475a2df8994c3a0e1b5a15dc692cbf5e8b97a50.png]
solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/337cb28fb01d27293af53cb76475a2df8994c3a0e1b5a15dc692cbf5e8b97a50.png] 

Radius of smaller circle = 5 units

Radius of larger circle = x units

Common tangent(AB) to both circles of length = 20 units

**Concept used:**

**Similar Triangle:**

Two triangles are said to be similar if they have the same ratio of corresponding sides and equal pairs of corresponding angles.

**In other words,** if two triangles have the same shape, but their sizes are different, then such triangles are called the similar triangle.

**Pythagoras theorem:**

**Hypotenuse = sqrt{(Perpendicular)² + (Base)²}**

**Calculation:**

By using pythagoras theorem,

CE = sqrt{(CA)² + (AE)²}

CE = sqrt{(5)² + (8)²} 

CE = sqrt{89} = 9.43 units

and,

ED = sqrt{(BE)² + (BD)²} 

ED = sqrt{(12)² + (x)²} .......(1)

From the figure, 

△ECA is similar to △EDB

Using the property of the similarity of a triangle,

(BD)/(AC)=(BE)/(AE)

(x)/(5)=(12)/(8)

x = (60)/(8)=7.5 units

Now, substituting the value of x in equation (1) we get,

ED = sqrt{(12)² + (7.5)²} 

ED = sqrt{200.25}= 14.15 units 

Distance between the centres of the two circles = CE + ED

= 9.43 + 14.15

= 23.58 units

Hence,** the correct answer is option 2)**.
